title: Vmysta ULUL 4-Day Hypertrophy & Strength
author: Vmysta
desc:
Goal / Purpose

This is an evidence-informed 4-day Upper/Lower hypertrophy program built for muscle growth, strength carryover, and sustainable recovery. It trains all major muscle groups through structured exercise selection, RIR-based progression, controlled volume, appropriate rest periods, and planned fatigue management.

This is not a quick-fix plan. It is for intermediate to advanced-intermediate lifters with solid technique who can train 4 days per week and use barbells, dumbbells, cables, machines, assisted pull-ups/dips, and hack squat or leg press alternatives.

Weekly structure:
Mon — Upper 1
Tue — Lower 1 + Core
Wed — Rest
Thu — Upper 2
Fri — Lower 2 + Core
Weekend — Rest / recovery

Sessions are demanding and usually last around 100–140 minutes depending on rest times, equipment availability, supersets, and execution quality.

Rep ranges generally vary from 5–20 reps. Most working sets are performed around 1–3 RIR (about RPE 7–9). Compounds stay more controlled, while safer isolation work can be pushed closer to failure when appropriate.

Progression: add reps within the target range first, then increase load once target reps are achieved with clean form and the intended RIR. If technique breaks down or performance drops too much after a load increase, keep the load and rebuild reps first.

Supersets: some exercises are intentionally paired for time efficiency. The higher-priority exercise is performed first. If equipment is unavailable or performance drops too much, perform the same exercises as straight sets. Quality reps, RIR, and progression matter more than rushing.

Loading: percentage-based loads on machines and isolation exercises are only rough guides. Prioritize clean technique, target reps, and RIR over strict %1RM targets.

Reactive deload: after up to 4 hard training weeks, deload when fatigue, performance, or recovery indicates it is needed. Keep the same exercises and order. Reduce sets as follows:
4→2
3→1
2→1
1→1

Use roughly 70% of previous working loads and target about RPE 7 (~3 RIR). No failure, grinders, or rep PRs.

Warm-up: use 5–10 min general preparation when needed and 1–3 progressive ramp-up sets before the first heavy compound. Warm-up sets do not count as working sets.

Rest: use about 3–4 min on major compounds, 2–3 min on accessory compounds, 90–120 sec on most isolation work, and 60–90 sec on smaller isolation/accessory movements. Extend rest when needed to preserve technique, reps, and intended RIR.

Results depend on consistency, nutrition, sleep, recovery, execution, and honest effort.
